classification.difficultyReason: Choose a sketch and both diagonals, find multiple isosceles/congruent subtriangles, introduce a common angle and link angle equations to derive all four angles without a supplied scaffold.

content.prompt: A quadrilateral. We are given a quadrilateral and are told that three of its sides are of equal length and the fourth side is the same length as each of the diagonals. Find the interior angles of the quadrilateral.

answer.worked:
Label the vertices in order so that $AB=BC=CD=s$ and $DA=AC=BD=t$, and draw both diagonals. Triangles $ABC$ and $DCB$ are congruent by SSS. Let $\theta=\angle BAC=\angle BCA=\angle CBD=\angle BDC$, using their isosceles base angles and congruence. Then $\angle ABC=180^\circ-2\theta$, so $\angle ABD=180^\circ-3\theta$.

As $AD=BD$, triangle $ABD$ is isosceles and $\angle BAD=180^\circ-3\theta$. Triangles $ABD$ and $DCA$ are congruent by SSS, so $\angle ACD=180^\circ-3\theta$. Since $AD=AC$, triangle $ACD$ has both base angles $180^\circ-3\theta$; hence $\angle DAC=6\theta-180^\circ$.

At $A$, $\angle BAD=\angle BAC+\angle CAD$, giving $180-3\theta=\theta+6\theta-180$, so $10\theta=360$ and $\theta=36^\circ$. Therefore $\angle A=\angle D=72^\circ$ and $\angle B=\angle C=108^\circ$.

spec.description: Authored convex solution sketch A/B/C/D with AB=BC=CD and AD=AC=BD, all six incidences; no numeric givens invented.
